name: Rules & Approvals
summary: Rules & Approvals is the workspace policy: it allows, refuses or holds other apps’ calls, always with a recorded reason.

intents: set a rule for my agents
require approval before an agent sends or pays
explain why a call was refused

operations.title: List rules
operations.description: List the workspace rules in evaluation order (priority, then newest first), the default mode that decides a call no rule matches, and the built-in system exemptions of that mode (read-only).

dynamicOps.description: `product.op` of every dynamic operation in the catalog (an operation that runs many tools); the "Allow always" link uses it to ask for one tool.

skipped.description: Releases whose manifest the last good index read could not use (for example a manifest URL that answered 404). The rest of the catalog is unaffected.

operations.title: Delete rule
operations.description: Remove a rule from evaluation. Its revision history stays.

operations.title: Restore a rule revision
operations.description: Make an earlier revision of a rule its current version, as a new revision. A deleted rule comes back. The revision passes the same checks as Save rule.

operations.title: Preview a decision
operations.description: Dry run: which rule would decide this call, and why. Optionally with an unsaved rule. The answer names the Fleet facts used (the caller's teams, the claimed requester's teams and trust) and whether they were available; when they are not, deny and hold rules that name them apply and allow rules that name them do not. For an app caller, pass its product (omit it to try a call whose product cannot be verified: deny and hold rules with callerProducts apply, allow rules with it do not). When no rule matches, the answer says what the default mode would do (pass `mode` to compare the three modes).

mode.description: Try the call under this default mode instead of the current one (dry run only; nothing changes).

operations.title: Check a rule against recent calls
operations.description: Runs a rule that is not saved yet over the last recorded gate decisions and answers which of those calls it would have matched and how the decision would change (before: what was decided then; after: what the rules, with this one, decide now). It uses only what the decision log keeps: no recipient handles, no Governance facts of that time. A rule that names recipients, the calling agent's teams or its trust cannot be checked and the answer says so. Nothing is stored. Reads that matched no rule are not in the log.

operations.title: Teams from Governance
operations.description: The replicated Governance teams and contact trust that rules can name, when they were last read, and whether Rules can rely on them now.

operations.title: Default mode and its history
operations.description: The default mode for calls that match no rule, who changed it last, its change history (newest first) and the built-in system exemptions.

operations.title: Set the default mode
operations.description: Set what happens to a call that matches no rule: permissive (allow), verification (hold for the owner) or closed (refuse). A move to a looser mode (closed, then verification, then permissive) needs confirm: true. Setting the current mode again changes nothing.

operations.title: Explain my decisions
operations.description: Why Rules allowed, refused or held your calls. Pass the callId of one call, or get your latest decisions. `decidedBy` says whether a rule or the workspace default mode (`mode`: permissive, verification or closed) decided.

operations.title: Draft rules from English
operations.description: Submit the owner's English rule together with your structured translation. It only creates a DRAFT; nothing applies until the owner approves it in the Rules app.
